areas.name: Downtown & Arts District
areas.character: The walkable centre — galleries, markets and the concert hall in one grid.
areas.summary: Warehouse galleries, a produce market and the concert hall sit within a short walk of each other.
stayIf: You want museums, food halls and rail on your doorstep
You’d rather not rent a car
skipIf: You picture quiet, leafy evenings
You’re here mainly for the beach

areas.name: Koreatown
areas.character: Dense, late-running and noticeably cheaper than the Westside.
areas.summary: The densest late-night grid in the city: barbecue, karaoke rooms and 24-hour cafés stacked several floors up.
stayIf: You want to eat late and pay less
You like being on a busy, central grid
skipIf: You need silence after midnight
You want to be near the coast

areas.name: Silver Lake & Echo Park
areas.character: Low-rise, hilly and independent — neighbourhood over landmark.
areas.summary: Hilly, walkable and low-rise — independent shops along Sunset Junction, a lake and stair-streets above it.
stayIf: You want cafés, shops and a genuine local feel
You’ve already ticked off the tourist sights
skipIf: You need flat, easy walking
You want big nightlife on the doorstep

areas.name: Hollywood
areas.character: The tourist spine, with rooms priced below the Westside.
areas.summary: The tourist spine — theatres, clubs and the Walk of Fame — with rooms priced below the Westside.
stayIf: You want landmarks within walking distance
It’s a short, first-time visit
skipIf: You want calm residential streets
You’d rather avoid the crowds

areas.name: West Hollywood
areas.character: Compact, design-led, and the city’s densest bar strip.
areas.summary: Design showrooms by day, the city’s densest bar strip by night, all inside a compact walkable grid.
stayIf: You want an evening out without driving between venues
You’ll make use of the walkable grid
skipIf: You’re holding a tight nightly budget
You need rail straight to downtown

areas.name: Santa Monica
areas.character: Beach, pier and a car-free week right on the coast.
areas.summary: Beach, pier and a pedestrian shopping street — the easiest part of the city to manage without a car.
stayIf: You’re travelling without a car
You want the beach at your door
skipIf: You’ll need to reach downtown often
The nightly rate is a stretch

areas.name: Venice
areas.character: Canals, skate park and a restaurant street — more lived-in than its neighbour.
areas.summary: Canals, a skate park and Abbot Kinney’s restaurants — more lived-in and cheaper than Santa Monica next door.
stayIf: You want beach mornings and a walkable food street
You prefer character over polish
skipIf: You want somewhere polished and tidy
You lean on late-night transit

areas.name: Culver City
areas.character: A small studio town with its own walkable downtown.
areas.summary: A small studio town with its own downtown: a few blocks of restaurants, a plaza, and quiet streets around it.
stayIf: You want rail access and a real neighbourhood
You want Westside proximity for less
skipIf: You want beach or an evening scene at the door
You’re after big-city buzz

areas.name: Beverly Hills & Mid-Wilshire
areas.character: Wide boulevards, museum row, and quiet by nine.
areas.summary: Wide boulevards, museum row and high-end retail; residential blocks are silent by nine.
stayIf: You want a calm base near the museums
The nightly rate fits comfortably
skipIf: You want somewhere still busy late in the evening
You’re watching the budget closely

areas.name: Studio City & NoHo
areas.character: Valley-side calm with a long restaurant boulevard and rail.
areas.summary: Valley-side residential streets with a long restaurant stretch on Ventura Blvd and the arts district by the station.
stayIf: You want budget with a train downtown
You don’t mind being over the hill
skipIf: You want to walk to the sights
You want beach access

areas.name: Pasadena
areas.character: A separate small city — Craftsman streets, gardens and a train in.
areas.summary: A separate small city — Craftsman architecture, gardens, and a walkable old town with a rail line into LA.
stayIf: You want walkable calm and a rail line
You like architecture and gardens
skipIf: You want to be central to LA
You’re here for the beach

areas.name: Central-Alameda & Vernon
areas.character: A working industrial district — warehouses and rail yards rather than storefronts.
areas.summary: Industrial blocks built around freight and manufacturing. Shops and restaurants are sparse, with long gaps between them.
stayIf: You have a specific reason to be right here
The lowest nightly rates outweigh being far from the sights
skipIf: You want shops, food or sights within walking distance
You want an easy trip without a car

areas.name: Habana Vieja
areas.character: The restored colonial core — plazas, cathedrals and museums packed into a few walkable blocks by the harbour.
stayIf: You want the headline sights outside your door
You'd rather walk everywhere than arrange rides
Restaurants, bars and live music within a few blocks matter
skipIf: Stretching your nightly budget further matters more to you than being in the middle of it
You need quiet to sleep — the streets stay lively late

areas.name: Centro Habana
areas.character: Dense, lived-in blocks between the old town and Vedado — everyday Havana rather than the postcard.
stayIf: You want the lowest nightly rates still within walking distance of the core
Staying among residents appeals more than staying among visitors
Being a short walk from both Habana Vieja and the Malecón suits you
skipIf: You want polished, restored surroundings rather than a working neighbourhood
You're set on stepping straight out into the main sights each morning

areas.name: Vedado
areas.character: Leafy mid-century avenues — grand hotels, jazz venues and a calmer pace set back from the crowds.
stayIf: You want a quieter base on tree-lined streets
A short ride into the old town each day works for you
You like cinemas, cafés and music venues spread around you
skipIf: You'd rather walk to the historic core than take a ride to it each time
You want to be in the thick of the old town, not a residential district

areas.name: Miramar
areas.character: Spacious embassy district across the river — large villas, private restaurants and room to breathe.
stayIf: You want space, calm and larger rooms over being central
You're happy to rely on taxis to reach the sights
Private restaurants and a residential feel appeal more than street bustle
skipIf: You want to reach the old town without depending on taxis
Being within walking distance of the main sights is important to you

sjo.note: Most trips treat San José as a short central stay before the coast or the volcanoes. Base yourself downtown, near Barrio Escalante, and it's walkable — there's no neighbourhood puzzle to solve here.

areas.name: Connaught Place & Central Delhi
areas.character: The white colonnades at the centre of New Delhi — three metro lines meet beneath it and the wide imperial avenues start at its edge.
stayIf: You want the metro network’s main interchange on your doorstep
You’re moving on to Agra or Jaipur and want the stations close
The museums and the government quarter are on your list
skipIf: You want restaurants and bars to walk to in the evening — the good ones are further south
You picture a leafy residential street rather than a commercial core

areas.name: Paharganj
areas.character: The budget bazaar facing New Delhi railway station — guesthouse stairwells, luggage shops and lanes too narrow for cars.
stayIf: You want the cheapest beds still within walking distance of the centre
You have an early train and want the platform close
Being in the middle of the noise is part of the appeal
skipIf: You want a quiet room and a lift
You’re arriving off a long flight and want somewhere calm to land
You’re carrying luggage you can’t wheel through crowded lanes

areas.name: Hauz Khas & South Delhi
areas.character: Where the city actually goes out — a ruined madrasa above a lake, design shops, and the densest run of restaurants and bars in Delhi.
stayIf: You want restaurants, bars and cafés rather than monuments at the door
You’d rather sleep somewhere residential and ride in to the sights
You’re here long enough that a metro ride each morning is no burden
skipIf: Your trip is three days of monuments and you want them close
You want to walk to the Red Fort and India Gate

areas.name: Aerocity
areas.character: A purpose-built block of international hotels beside the airport — a few restaurants inside it and nothing at all outside.
stayIf: You have a pre-dawn flight or a long layover
You want a predictable international hotel and a short transfer
skipIf: You came to see Delhi — everything worth seeing is a long ride away
You want to step outside and find a street to wander

areas.name: Nizamuddin & Lodhi
areas.character: Mughal tombs and gardens on one side, a working shrine quarter on the other — the calmest central base in the city.
stayIf: You want gardens and tombs on your morning walk
You want to be central without being in the commercial crush
Qawwali at the shrine on a Thursday evening appeals
skipIf: You want somewhere that stays busy into the evening
You’re counting every rupee on the room

areas.name: Downtown & Business Bay
areas.character: The Burj Khalifa, the fountain and the mall — the city’s postcard, with a canal and a wall of towers behind it.
stayIf: You want the headline sights and the largest mall on your doorstep
A metro station and the fountain show within walking distance matter
skipIf: You came for the beach — it’s a long ride from here
You want streets to wander rather than podiums and skybridges

areas.name: Dubai Marina & JBR
areas.character: Towers packed around a man-made marina with a beach promenade behind them — the one part of the city built to be walked.
stayIf: You want the beach and a walkable evening strip in the same place
You’d rather not take a taxi to dinner
You’ll use the metro and the tram rather than taxis
skipIf: You’re here mainly for the creek and the souks
High-rise density isn’t what you pictured

areas.name: Deira & Bur Dubai
areas.character: The creek, the gold and spice souks and the abra crossings — the oldest part of the city and the cheapest to sleep in.
stayIf: You want the lowest nightly rates and the oldest streets
You’d rather walk souks than malls
Crossing the water by abra each day appeals
skipIf: You want a beach within walking distance
You pictured glass towers and new-build hotels

areas.name: Al Barsha & Barsha Heights
areas.character: Mid-rise apartment blocks around a big mall — where the value rooms are, on the metro line but off the postcard.
stayIf: You want space and a low rate with the metro still at hand
You’re happy to commute to both the beach and the old city
skipIf: You’d rather not start and end each day with a commute
It’s a short trip and you’d rather be central

areas.name: Jumeirah & Umm Suqeim
areas.character: Low villa streets along the best public beaches, under the sail of the Burj Al Arab.
stayIf: You want beach mornings and low-rise streets
You’d rather have a resort than a tower
skipIf: You’d rather not rely on taxis for every trip — the metro doesn’t reach here
You want city sights and an evening scene close by

areas.name: Centro Storico
areas.character: The Pantheon, Navona and the Trevi inside one knot of lanes — you open the door and you are already there.
stayIf: You want the sights themselves, not a neighbourhood to discover
It’s a short trip and walking everywhere matters more than the rate
skipIf: You’re holding a tight nightly budget
You want a room away from crowds and late-night noise

areas.name: Trastevere
areas.character: Cobbled lanes and ivy on the far bank — a restaurant on every corner and a hill of gardens above them.
stayIf: You want dinner and an evening walk without crossing the city
You’d rather stay in a neighbourhood than inside a monument
skipIf: You’re relying on the metro to get around
You want to be asleep early on a Friday

areas.name: Monti
areas.character: A village of workshops and wine bars wedged between the Forum and the hill — central, but quiet by Roman standards.
stayIf: You want the Forum and the Colosseum on foot and a real neighbourhood at night
You prefer small shops and wine bars to big restaurants
skipIf: You want the Vatican side close
Steep cobbled streets are a problem for you

areas.name: Prati & the Vatican
areas.character: Wide nineteenth-century blocks behind St Peter’s — orderly, well fed, and one bridge from the old centre.
stayIf: You want the Vatican first thing and calm streets afterwards
You’d like more room for your money than the centre gives
skipIf: You want the Forum and the Colosseum within walking distance
You want tangled old lanes rather than a grid

areas.name: Termini & Esquilino
areas.character: The transport hub — every train, bus and airport link, with the cheapest central rooms clustered around it.
stayIf: You want the lowest central rates and every onward connection
You’re using Rome as a base for day trips
skipIf: You want the street outside to be part of the holiday
It’s a short trip and you want to walk to everything

areas.name: Downtown & Coal Harbour
areas.character: Glass towers between two shorelines — the seawall on one side, the shopping streets on the other.
stayIf: You want the seawall and the ferries at the door
You’re not renting a car
skipIf: You want a neighbourhood rather than a downtown
The nightly rate is a stretch

areas.name: West End & Davie
areas.character: Leafy low-rise blocks between the park and the beach — the residential, walkable side of downtown.
stayIf: You want Stanley Park and English Bay on your morning walk
You want to stay central without paying the tower rate
skipIf: You’ll have a car and need somewhere easy to park it
Your trip is built around the convention centre or a cruise departure

areas.name: Gastown & Chinatown
areas.character: The oldest brick streets in the city — cobbles, restored warehouses and the densest run of restaurants downtown.
stayIf: You want restaurants, bars and the SkyTrain within a few blocks
You like old brick and cobblestone over glass
skipIf: You picture beach mornings rather than brick streets
Cobbles and a busy street late on aren’t what you pictured

areas.name: Kitsilano
areas.character: Wooden houses above a swimming beach, with a long street of cafés and outdoor shops behind them.
stayIf: You want a beach, a pool and a neighbourhood to walk in
You’d rather look at downtown across the water than stand in it
skipIf: You want to walk to downtown rather than ride
It’s a two-night trip and you want to be central

areas.name: Mount Pleasant & Main Street
areas.character: Brew halls, vintage shops and low-rise blocks along Main — the best value anywhere near the centre.
stayIf: You want the lowest rates while still being close in
You’d rather eat and drink where the city does
skipIf: You want water views or the seawall
You want the sights within walking distance

areas.name: Vieux-Québec, Haute-Ville
areas.character: Inside the walls and under the Château — stone streets, ramparts, and the boardwalk terrace above the river.
stayIf: You want the walled city outside your door
It’s a short trip and the setting matters more than the rate
skipIf: You’re watching the nightly rate closely
Steep streets and stairs are a problem for you

areas.name: Petit-Champlain & Vieux-Port
areas.character: The lower town at the foot of the cliff — the narrowest street in the old city, a market hall, and the river ferry.
stayIf: You want the old-town postcard and the waterfront in one place
The market and the ferry on foot appeal
skipIf: You’d rather not climb between upper and lower town several times a day
You want the lowest rates in the city

areas.name: Saint-Roch
areas.character: The flat lower-town grid that became the city’s restaurant and design quarter — no ramparts, no tour groups.
stayIf: You want the best eating and the lowest rates in one place
You’d rather have flat streets than a hill
You’re staying long enough to want a neighbourhood
skipIf: You came for the walled city and want to wake up inside it
It’s one night and you want the postcard

areas.name: Montcalm & Saint-Jean-Baptiste
areas.character: Grande Allée’s terraces, the battlefield park, and quiet residential streets immediately outside the walls.
stayIf: You want the old town on foot but a residential street to sleep on
You’ll use the Plains of Abraham for running or skiing
skipIf: You want to be inside the walls
You want the waterfront and the ferry close
